findings.text: Per-CPU context tracking record holds an optional user activation flag with recursion depth, an atomic combined state word, and optional idle nesting counters for process context and for interrupt and NMI context. Each member is present only under its corresponding build option for user tracking, generic tracking, or idle tracking.

Execution context is classified into disabled unknown, kernel, idle, user, and guest values bounded by a maximum sentinel. Kernel is the quiescent value, user and guest denote non-kernel execution bracketed by entry and exit announcements, idle is a distinct quiescent mode, and disabled is reported when tracking is unavailable rather than representing live execution.

User boundary announcements are offered in normal and interrupt-disabled forms for entering and leaving user execution. In disabled builds they are empty and report neutral values, while in available builds they act only when globally enabled and otherwise delegate to internal transition helpers with the user selector.

Exception boundary handling preserves the prior context across the exception. Entry reports a neutral value when off-stack user tracking is selected or tracking is globally disabled, leaves kernel execution unannounced, and announces departure from non-kernel execution. Exit re-announces only a saved non-kernel context under the complementary configuration.

Guest boundary announcements bracket virtualized execution with the guest selector. Available variants announce only when globally enabled and then report the per-CPU enabled state, while disabled variants perform no announcement and report not enabled.

A global enable predicate gates all tracking actions. One configuration hard-wires it and its per-CPU refinements to negative with state readers returning unknown or neutral values, while the enabled configuration refines the global check with a per-CPU active flag for current-CPU and selected-CPU queries.

State sampling that must not migrate holds preemption disabled across the per-CPU state read. The RCU warning path uses the notrace form of disable and enable so diagnostic reporting that itself depends on RCU state does not recurse.

The atomic state word packs a low context field and a higher RCU watching field. Total width derives from the storage size, the context field is sized to represent the maximum context value starting at bit zero, the watching field starts immediately above it with full remaining width except under torture builds, and masks plus residual unused width are exposed.

RCU watching status is queryable for the current CPU and for an explicitly selected CPU, including an acquire-ordered variant, by masking the atomic state word. A current-CPU predicate tests the watching bit and a separate primitive atomically adds to the same word.

Idle tracking exposes process nesting and interrupt and NMI nesting counters for the current CPU and for a selected CPU. A large sentinel above half the signed long range marks the non-idle interrupt nesting value.

The RCU warning helpers ensure diagnostic code observes watching state. Entry reports whether it temporarily forced watching on, and exit reverses only a forced transition. A disabled configuration hard-wires entry to negative and exit to empty.

Idle and interrupt and NMI transition announcements are empty operations in the routed configuration, covering idle enter and exit, interrupt enter and exit in both interrupt-state flavors, and NMI enter and exit, together with an empty global initialization operation.

Conditional warning support evaluates its tested condition together with the enabled predicate in the active configuration and compiles to nothing in the disabled configuration, so callers must not rely on side effects of the tested expression.

Cookie generation uses a per-CPU record holding nesting depth and last value with sixteen-byte alignment, and a shared generator holding a per-CPU pointer plus forward and reverse sixty-four-bit counters with cacheline separation for the forward counter. A batch constant spaces per-CPU allocation and a definition helper instantiates both pieces zero-initialized.

The cookie allocator promises distinct values across CPUs and reentrant use. The common case reuses a per-CPU sequence with whole-batch refill from a shared forward counter on multiprocessor builds at batch boundaries, while reentrant use draws from an oppositely moving shared reverse counter, with nesting depth selecting the path.
Cookie generation uses no sleeping lock. It isolates the fast path with a per-CPU nesting counter and shares batches and the reentrant sequence through atomic sixty-four-bit counters.

Core dump metadata describes each mapping by address range, flags, dump size, file offset, and backing file. Dump parameters snapshot the triggering signal, output file, size limit, memory filtering flags, dumpability, CPU, progress offsets, mapping count and array, and target process identifier.

Coredump diagnostics provide informational and failure reporting flavors. One configuration logs the current task identity with rate limiting, while another compiles reports away and reduces filesystem dump and safety validation entry points to empty operations.

Common Platform Error Record header ABI fixes a four-character signature and its length, an all-bits-set end sentinel, a record revision, a fixed record length, a four-level severity ordering from recoverable through fatal and corrected to informational, and validity bits for platform identifier, timestamp, and partition identifier.

Notification types for corrected machine check, corrected platform error, machine check, PCI express, initialization, non-maskable interrupt, boot, and DMA remapping events are each assigned distinct persistent GUID identifiers.

Error section types covering Compute Express Link protocol, general media, DRAM, and memory module errors, generic and architecture-specific processor errors, platform memory, PCI express, firmware reference, PCI-X bus, PCI device, generic DMA remapping, virtualization-technology DMA remapping, and IOMMU DMA remapping are each assigned distinct persistent GUID identifiers.

Section ABI fixes hardware error flag bits for recovered, previous-error, and simulated conditions, a section revision, field-valid bits for replaceable-unit identity and text, and attribute bits for primary, containment warning, reset, threshold exceeded, resource inaccessible, and latent error.

Section payloads use validity bitmaps for processor, memory, PCI express, and ARM fields. Processor coverage includes type, instruction set, error kind, operation, flags, level, version, brand, identifier, addresses, routing, and instruction pointer. Memory coverage includes status, addresses, topology, geometry, identifiers, extended handles, and row extension, bank address, and chip identifier packing. PCI express coverage includes port, version, status, identity, serial, bridge, capability, AER data, and slot decoding. ARM coverage includes processor identity, affinity, running state, vendor data, and per-record presence.
Each routed header defines a once-only inclusion guard so repeated inclusion is idempotent.
